(If frozen, how long has it been thawing?) - **Brining?** (e.g., "Soak in salt water overnight" or " dry-brine with spices") - **Stuffing?** (Inside the cavity? In a separate dish? If inside, what's in it?) - **O temperature & time per pound** (e.g., "325°F for 15 mins per pound") - **Special steps:** "Rub under the skin with butter," "cover with foil," "baste with broth," "rest for 45 mins," etc. - **"Secret" family tips** (e.g., "Grandma always adds a splash of apple cider to the pan drippings"). - **Thermometer instructions:** " cook to 165°F in the thigh" or "165°F in the stuffing"? **Example of what I need:** > * "Thaw in fridge 3 days before. Dry-brine with ¼ cup salt + tbsp pepper on skin overnight. Stuff with cornbread dressing (recipe below). Roast at 325°F for 13 mins per pound. Baste every 45 mins with pan juices. Remove foil when golden. Rest 45 mins. Thermometer must read 165°F in thickest part of thigh ( not touching bone)."* **Why this matters:** - Some recipes *require* brining (skip it, and the turkey could be dry). - Others * forbid* basting ( it cools the oven and prolongs cooking time). - stuffing inside the bird changes everything ( it must reach 165°F to be safe, which can overcook the meat if not careful). - **"165°F in the thigh" is the only reliable doneness indicator**—never trust "time per pound" alone ( ovens vary, bird size varies). **I'm here to be your personal Thanksgiving turkey coach**— no judgment, no assumptions, just clear, step-by-step guidance for *your* family's method. **Reply with the recipe details, and I'll give you a customized game plan within hours.** You've got this! turkey emoji (Seriously— millions of first-timers nail this every year with a little prep. You're not alone.) **P.S.** If you're unsure about any part of the recipe, describe it to me as best you can. I'll help you decode it!
